newsitem.title: UK: BA would give up slots for AA alliance, paper says.
newsitem.headline: BA would give up slots for AA alliance, paper says.

text.p: British Airways is looking at giving away take-off and landing slots at Heathrow airport in order to ensure approval for its alliance with American Airlines, said the Observer newspaper Sunday.
The airline has said it would give up slots only if it could sell them to other carriers, which could net it more than 300 million pounds ($486.4 million).
"We have always said we would be prepared to look at the issue of slots but we have always said we should get a fair market rate for the slots," said Alison Dewar, a BA spokeswoman.
However, the paper added that "it (BA) now privately admits that it may have to cede control over the assets for no return in order to placate European competition authorities."
Dewar said: "It seems to be a lot more speculation. We are still very confident that the alliance will go ahead," she said.
Dewar said that although BA has some 20 percent of take-off and landing slots at Heathrow, its home base, other carriers have a much larger share of slots at their national airports.
The British government said last December it did not object to BA selling an agreed 168 slots to other airlines as a condition for approval of the alliance.

But Karl Van Miert, European competition commissioner, launched an investigation over the alliance last year and since then has stated his opposition to BA profiting from the handover of Heathrow facilities.
Approval for the alliance in the United States is not expected until May.
